source.title: CALIBURN: Self-Calibrated LLM Unlearning Alignment
source.authors: Zheng-Bang Yang; Yisheng Zhong; Junyuan Hong; Zhuangdi Zhu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. There are minor PDF extraction and table-layout artifacts, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a held-out extraction-oriented role-play prompt recovers Harry Potter knowledge after unlearning. This is a different attack from the claim's other recovery methods.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests extraction-oriented prompting on unlearned models. It also reports unlearning and utility outcomes used to assess the tested method. Attacks mentioned only as prior work in the related-work discussion are not study results and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.14 applies a held-out role-play extraction prompt to Llama3.2-3B models unlearned with NPO+KL, WGA+KL, FLAT and CALIBURN+KL. It reports Harry Potter memorization scores, which bear directly on prompt-only recovery (E), on whether unlearning holds up (A), and on a new method's claimed robustness (F). This is a different attack aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In addition, the authors state that the role-play prompt successfully elicits the target knowledge from NPO and WGA, and that FLAT also suppresses extraction but with substantial utility loss. They claim CALIBURN is robust only to this one extraction-oriented prompt.
record.recipe_differences: CALIBURN is a distinct self-calibrated, token-level unlearning objective. The recovery test is a held-out role-play prompt, not fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization.
record.method_sensitivity: The attack outcome varies by unlearning method and evaluation set: the prompt raises WGA scores substantially on Extended and more modestly on MUSE, but does not raise CALIBURN+KL scores.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Attack evidence is limited to one held-out role-play extraction prompt and Harry Potter evaluation. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The WMDP outcomes do not state a chance reference. The paper does not test fine-tuning, internal-edit, or quantization attacks.
record.rows_left_out: The paper contains additional method-comparison and benchmark results in Tables 1-2 and Appendix A.8-A.10. The rows retained focus on the tested prompt attack and CALIBURN outcomes; the remaining method-by-metric comparison entries are not individually transcribed.

untested.parts: Simple attacks other than one role-play prompt, and any attack on the WMDP-unlearned models.
Entire version: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Entire version: no activation ablation or probing of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
Other languages, in-context information, multiple rephrasings, and other jailbreaks. Only one prompt, one model (3B) and one task (Harry Potter) were tested.
Robustness of CALIBURN to fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, other prompts, the WMDP setting, and the larger models.

missing.what: Prompted base-model control: Llama3.2-3B scores 40.58 (Extended) and 28.84 (MUSE) under the prompt, against 39.99 and 32.13 under standard evaluation. This is the right baseline for judging how much recovery the prompt gives.
MMLU under the prompt for FLAT (50.12), which shows FLAT's resistance comes with a utility cost.

record.verdict_notes: Attack evidence comes from a single prompt, a single 3B model and a single task, with no uncertainty reported. NPO+KL barely unlearned before the attack, so its recovery says little. The MMLU values in Table 16 appear copied from Table 2. The WMDP rows describe the method's own performance with no attack applied.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests benchmarked forgetting and utility, including under one held-out extraction-oriented prompt; it does not test the full range of simple attacks named in the claim.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or test showing that knowledge is blocked from access rather than deleted. The paper analyzes its own gradient weighting, not that mechanism.
Tests one held-out role-play extraction prompt. Does not test other languages, in-context information, or a broader range of prompt rephrasings and jailbreaks.
Tests CALIBURN against the held-out role-play extraction prompt only, not fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, or the broader set of attacks in the claim.

rows.operation_detail: Applied held-out role-play extraction prompt to the unlearned model.
rows.note: The authors say the prompt elicits target knowledge in NPO. The reported increase over standard evaluation is limited.
rows.check: The state should be observed, not partial. NPO+KL rises from 33.62 to 39.69, essentially the prompted base value of 40.58. The prompt therefore recovers all of the small amount NPO+KL had removed. Note that NPO+KL unlearned little to begin with (base 39.99).

relation.reason: Table 16 reports prompt-only recovery results for several unlearned models.

tranche.reason: Different method (CALIBURN), same question: prompt-only recovery tested on its own and other methods, Appendix A.14.

source_check.notes: The only attack is one held-out role-play prompt (Appendix A.14, Table 16) on Llama3.2-3B-Instruct Harry Potter models. It raises the base on Extended (39.99 to 40.58) and lowers it on MUSE (32.13 to 28.84), so compare with the prompted base. All Table 16 MMLU values repeat Table 2. The WMDP rows (Zephyr, Table 1) have no attack. The EMNLP 2026 venue comes from record metadata; the text shows only arXiv v3.

statements.correction: Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, Harry Potter raw-text unlearning, MUSE-protocol Know f: CALIBURN+KL is 0.00 on Extended and MUSE both with and without one held-out role-play prompt. MMLU is 59.48 against base 60.45 (Table 16, Table 2). The authors tested their own method with one prompt they chose.
statements.problem: Cites R7 but gives none of this study's results. Its conditions (WMDP MCQ and TOFU) and why-list leave out this study's Harry Potter/MUSE setting and role-play prompt.

statements.correction: Same held-out role-play prompt, Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, Harry Potter Extended: WGA+KL rises 13.31 to 37.59 (prompted base 40.58), while CALIBURN+KL stays 0.00 to 0.00. Also NPO+KL 33.62 to 39.69 and FLAT 5.44 to 1.13 (Table 2, Table 16).
statements.problem: Cites R3 and R7 but gives none of this study's results. The contrast they show does fit the factor (same prompt, different methods).

statements.correction: CALIBURN+KL (proposed in this paper) stays 0.00 on Harry Potter Extended and MUSE under one held-out role-play prompt chosen by its authors (Llama3.2-3B-Instruct). FLAT, a baseline from other authors, falls 5.44 to 1.13 and 6.35 to 0.40, with MMLU 50.12 against 60.45.
statements.problem: Cites R5-R8 but describes nothing from this study. FLAT (R5, R6) is a prior method (Wang et al. 2025b) used here as a baseline, so it does not fit 'attacked by their own authors'. Only CALIBURN (R7, R8) fits.

statements.correction: WGA+KL goes 13.31 to 37.59 (Extended, prompted base 40.58) and 19.70 to 27.09 (MUSE, prompted base 28.84). That is about 93% and 94% of the prompted base. Both are test sets for the same Harry Potter forget target, and Extended includes the raw MUSE samples (Table 2 caption).
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but Extended and MUSE are two test sets for the same Harry Potter target, and Extended includes the MUSE samples. So they are not different domains or concepts. The bigger rise on Extended tracks its higher prompted base (40.58 vs 28.84) and larger starting gap.

statements.correction: CALIBURN+KL (Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, Harry Potter raw text, KL retention) keeps Know f at 0.00 on Extended and MUSE under one held-out role-play prompt, with MMLU 59.48 against 60.45 (Table 16). This is the authors' own test of their own method with a single prompt. Code is released.
statements.problem: Cites R7 and R8 but gives none of this study's results. Its conditions (WMDP, TOFU, DUET; translation, wrappers, paraphrase, sampling) and why ('All four are preprints') leave this study out. The record lists it as EMNLP 2026 with code.
